mechanism: A privacy-preserving communication protocol where sensitive content is not encrypted into noise, but mapped to a Cover Domain via structural analogy. The agent uses an {{analogy_bridge}} to translate the sensitive Source (e.g., a proprietary trading strategy) into a structurally corresponding Target narrative (e.g., a logistics optimization problem). To an external observer, the {{message}} appears as valid, low-entropy text about the Target domain. The receiver, possessing the specific Bridge Key (mapping dictionary), inverts the analogy to recover the structural intent. It requires an initial {{ontology_handshake}} to securely establish the shared Bridge Key before transmission begins. Primary use cases: sanitizing proprietary information for external review, translating classified operational plans into unclassified training analogues, and privacy-preserving inter-organizational coordination.
gloss: Privacy-preserving communication via approximate domain translation
failure_modes: Mapping leakage (if the analogy is too perfect, the cover text becomes suspicious).
Lossy translation (nuance lost in the bridge — reconstruction is approximate, not exact).
Non-deterministic reconstruction: same bridge key applied twice may yield different interpretations.
Analogy collapse: Cover Domain lacks sufficient structural complexity to represent Payload.
invariants: Cover Coherence: The output text must be semantically valid in the Cover Domain
Structural Correspondence: Key relations in Payload must have counterparts in Cover (correspondence is approximate, not guaranteed bijective)
preconditions: Cover Domain has sufficient structural complexity to represent core Payload relations
postconditions: Receiver can reconstruct structural intent (with acknowledged fidelity loss)
